thread.title: Mountain View resident arrested in connection with fire at historic Buddhist monastery

author: r. r. rockwell
title: Mountain View resident arrested in connection with fire at historic Buddhist monastery
text:
The Monterey County Sheriff’s Office announced on June 3 that a Ramey warrant has been issued and served for 36-year-old GuoGuo Lu of Mountain View, California. Lu was arrested in connection with the investigation into the March 27, 2026, fire at the Tassajara Zen Mountain Center located at 39171 Tassajara Road in Carmel Valley. The center is recognized as the oldest Japanese Buddhist Soto Zen monastery in the United States.
According to authorities, deputies began investigating after discovering public online statements linking Lu to the fire and threats of future violence against Buddhist temples across California. At present, Lu is incarcerated at Napa County Jail on unrelated charges and awaits extradition to Monterey County. The sheriff’s office said there is no indication that she poses an ongoing threat to the public.
Sheriff Tina Nieto said, “The Monterey County Sheriff’s Office remains committed to protecting every member of our community and ensuring that all people can safely practice their faith without fear of violence, intimidation, or threats. We take allegations involving crimes motivated by bias or hatred very seriously and will continue to work diligently to investigate these incidents and hold those responsible accountable under the law.”
The sheriff’s office expressed gratitude toward staff and faculty at Tassajara Zen Center for their quick actions during the incident. Their cooperation aided investigators and helped prevent further harm. Fire personnel were also commended for responding promptly despite challenging conditions posed by remote access, distance, and limited communications.
Lu faces charges including terrorizing by destructive device or arson (11413 PC), arson (451 PC), criminal threats (422 PC), and committing a felony hate crime (422.75 PC). Her bail has been set at $130,000. The investigation remains active; authorities are asking anyone with information about this incident or related social media posts or threats directed toward Buddhist religious institutions to contact Deputy Aly Najem or Deputy Kyle Massa at 831-755-5111, or submit an anonymous tip via the sheriff’s office website.
